notes:
STAYED RED: j1 'Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.' is
Mark 8:26, Jesus speaking in the flesh, and a red-letter KJV prints it red. It had
no evangelist framing welded onto it, so no split was needed. It keeps its id and
its still.

LIFTED - THE BLIND MAN'S OWN LINE. The whole point of this story is the sentence
the man says between the two touches, and it was narrator paraphrase: n2 read
'he could see, but only halfway. People looked like trees walking around.' That is
Mark 8:24 and the KJV records the man saying it himself:
  s24  Mark 8:24  'I see men as trees, walking.'  SCRIPTURE, light blue.
He is a man in the story, not Deity, so blue is right. n2 keeps its original text
and now works as the retelling directly after him, on the SAME still (ST4), so the
picture the viewer sees does not change.

ADDED RETELLING: j1 was the last beat, which left the only Old English line in the
video with nobody to say it again. n5 is new and retells it on ST7, the still j1
already sits on.

NOTE ON THE ORDER: the brief's `segments` list had j1 before n4 while `beats` had
it after. The beat order is what renders, so the segment list is now written in
beat order. No ids changed.

WOMEN: Mark 8:22-26 records no woman speaking. Nothing added; nothing invented.

WHY-LAW: Jesus was not short on power at the first touch. Half-sight was allowed
to exist for a moment. Milk framing - a faith that comes in stages is still his
work, and he is patient enough to lay hands on you twice.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Friends brought a blind man to Jesus in Bethsaida and begged Him just to touch him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus took the man by the hand and walked him outside the village.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He spit on the man's eyes and laid His hands on him, then asked if he could see anything yet.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: I see men as trees, walking.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The man looked up and said the strangest thing — he could see, but only halfway. People looked like trees walking around.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus put His hands on the man's eyes a second time and told him to look up again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And this time he saw everything clearly — every face, every leaf. The second touch finished what the first had started.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Don't go back into the town, Jesus told him, and don't tell anybody there. The healing was for the man himself — not for a crowd to talk about.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Maybe your faith came in stages too. He is patient enough to touch you twice.

stills_wanted.ST4: ST4 now carries the man's verbatim line AND its retelling. Frame the half-sight itself, from close beside him: the man's face turned up, eyes open and straining, a blurred smear of standing figures in the middle distance that genuinely read as trunks and branches. Wonder and confusion at once - he is seeing, and it is not right yet.
stills_wanted.ST7: ST7 now carries Jesus's only spoken line and its retelling. Frame the quiet dismissal on the road outside the village: Jesus close, hand still resting on the healed man's shoulder, speaking low, the town small and far behind them. Private, unhurried, no onlookers - the opposite of a crowd.
